paper_metadata.title: Effect of thermomechanical processing history on microstructural evolution and fracture mechanisms in NbTaTiHf refractory medium-entropy alloy

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: This study examines how processing history governs microstructural evolution and tensile fracture behavior in the NbTaTiHf RMEA.

evidence.section: 2. Experimental procedures
evidence.quote: The NbTaTiHf cast ingot was prepared by cold crucible induction melting (CCIM) of equimolar mixtures of the corresponding elements in an argon atmosphere.

parameters.atmosphere: high-purity argon with continuous flow rate of 100 mL/min

evidence.section: 2. Experimental procedures
evidence.quote: the billet was homogenized in a heating furnace at 1260 ◦C (1533 K) for 30 min, covered with Ti foil.

parameters.atmosphere: argon flow directed at the sample surface
parameters.deformation: final thickness reduction ~75% after seven passes

other.rolling_mill: laboratory-scale Φ450 mm unidirectional rolling mill

evidence.section: 2. Experimental procedures
evidence.quote: Hot rolling was subsequently performed on a laboratory-scale Φ 450 mm unidirectional rolling mill, with an initial rolling temperature of approximately 1200 ◦C, and the rolling process was performed with argon flow directed at the sample surface. After seven passes of hot rolling, the final thickness reduction of the sheet was about 75%.

parameters.cooling_method: cooling at a constant rate of 15 °C/min to room temperature

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure characterization and uniaxial tensile property of as-cast ingot

evidence.section: 3.2.3 Fracture surface morphology of hot-rolled and annealed sheet
evidence.quote: The XRD patterns indicate that only the BCC phase was detected at each annealing temperature, and no significant differences in the peak positions or intensity ratios were observed across the different annealing conditions.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure characterization and uniaxial tensile property of as-cast ingot
evidence.quote: Typical equiaxed grains with a size of ~100 μm with intergranular and intragranular pores can be recognized on the surface.

attributes.size: equivalent diameter 4.5 µm to 64 µm; some linear dimension ~100 µm

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure characterization and uniaxial tensile property of as-cast ingot
evidence.quote: shrinkage pores are uniformly distributed within the specimen, with a total volume fraction of 0.038% and the linear dimension of some pores is around 100 μm.

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Microstructure characterizations of hot-rolled and annealed sheet
evidence.quote: severely deformed grains exhibit well-defined deformation bands.

attributes.morphology: band-like structures with rotation axis <110>; misorientation varying

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Microstructure characterizations of hot-rolled and annealed sheet
evidence.quote: suggesting that the band-like structures represent kink bands with a rotation axis aligned along <110>.

attributes.size: length scale roughly comparable to grain size

evidence.section: 3.2.3 Fracture surface morphology of hot-rolled and annealed sheet
evidence.quote: the fracture surface shows a mixed appearance and contains a number of microcracks, as shown in Fig. 13 (e), with a length scale roughly comparable to the grain size.

evidence.section: 3.2.3 Fracture surface morphology of hot-rolled and annealed sheet
evidence.quote: the three-dimensional morphology of individual recrystallized grains is clearly visible on the fracture surface, arising from extensive intergranular cracking.

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Microstructure characterizations of hot-rolled and annealed sheet
evidence.quote: After hot rolling and annealing at 1000 ◦C for 1 h, the mean grain size reduces to 19 μm with more than 90% below 35 μm.

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Microstructure characterizations of hot-rolled and annealed sheet
evidence.quote: When the annealing temperature rises to 1300 ◦C and 1400 ◦C, the mean grain size increases to 51 μm and 64 μm respectively.
